PHASE D rationale for ABSENT over OUT_OF_SCOPE (supersedes the Phase C NOTE above, which is retained verbatim for provenance): (a) the frozen taxonomy explicitly steers size/foundations items away from OUT_OF_SCOPE; (b) the library already has an established idiom for exactly the missing ingredient -- smallness supplied as explicit DATA rather than as machinery: Adjunction/SAFT.v packages well-poweredness and the cogenerator as `SubobjectIndex`/`Cogenerator` precisely 'since the library has no smallness/image-factorization machinery', and Theory/WeaklyInitial.v deliberately keeps its endomorphism-indexed product an explicit input 'so that ... the universe constraints remain in the caller's hands'; (c) the library's parametric/conditional-theorem pattern (docs/INHABITATION.md) is designed for results whose distinctive premise has no in-tree model, and the classical/cardinality step could be a hypothesis of exactly that kind, in an Instance-layer file where docs/AXIOMS.md already sanctions stdlib axioms. The item is hard and low-value, but it is not 'not meaningfully formalizable in this library's setting'.

verifier.notes: Blind pass (done before reading the coverage file) reached ABSENT independently and found exactly the same in-tree material Phase C found: two header essays (Structure/Complete.v:64-70 and :102-106, Adjunction/GAFT.v:105) that STATE Freyd's collapse in prose with citations, and no proof-carrying constant anywhere. Phase C's factual findings are all confirmed -- the library has no smallness predicate, no cardinality apparatus, and the header does say the thinness theorem 'cannot be proved constructively'. What is overturned is only the taxonomy call. The frozen definition reserves OUT_OF_SCOPE for what is 'not meaningfully formalizable in this library's setting' and warns in the same breath that size/foundations items are usually PARTIAL or PRESENT because the library has universe polymorphism. Decisive here is the in-tree PRECEDENT: this library's answer to 'no smallness machinery' is not 'out of scope', it is 'pass the smallness as data' -- Adjunction/SAFT.v (SubobjectIndex, Cogenerator) and Theory/WeaklyInitial.v (endomorphism-indexed product kept an explicit input) both do exactly that, and docs/INHABITATION.md records the library's habit of proving flagship results as axiom-free conditionals over premises with no in-tree model. Under that idiom Freyd's proposition is statable and conditionally provable; it is simply unformalized. Hence ABSENT. Phase E guidance carried over from Phase C and endorsed: this should NOT become an ordinary 'formalize theorem X' issue. If filed at all, scope it as (i) stating the collapse conditionally over an explicit size/classicality hypothesis pack in an Instance-layer file, or (ii) recording it as a documented boundary; the Hyland counterexample means no unconditional core-theory proof is possible.

statement_record.intree: Cat_Closed supplies exactly the adjunct passage: exp_iso : (A ∏ B ⟶ C) ≊ (A ⟶ [B, C]), with `to` the currying x ↦ (y ↦ F (x, y)), `from` the uncurrying, and both round-trip laws proved (the header records the instance is closed under the global context, no axioms). statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the adjunct passage (the currying isomorphism is in-tree in full, in both directions, with the exponential UMP); intree-weaker for E_p: no functor `[P, X] ⟶ X` evaluating at a fixed object p is defined anywhere. The nearest in-tree constants are the two-variable `eval` at Cat and `ev1` (Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v:83), which evaluates at ONE designated object of ONE designated functor category restricted to the model subcategory.

statement_record.book: Let S : J -> X^P be such that for every object p of P the composite E_p S : J -> X has a limit L_p with limiting cone tau_p. Then there is a UNIQUE functor L : P -> X with object function p |-> L_p making p |-> tau_p a natural transformation tau : Delta L => S, and this tau is a limiting cone in X^P. Equivalently E_p(Lim S) = Lim(E_p S): limits in a functor category are computed pointwise when the pointwise limits exist.
statement_record.intree: Functor_Category_Cartesian : @Cartesian D → @Cartesian (@Fun C D), with (F × G) c := F c × G c on objects, split (fmap[F] f) (fmap[G] f) on arrows, projections/pairing componentwise, and ump_products inherited pointwise from D.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three separate ways: (1) SHAPE — only the discrete two-object diagram (binary products); no general index category J, and not even the empty diagram (there is no Terminal instance for [C, D]), so not even finite products in [C, D] follow; (2) FORM — the book's clause that the functor structure on p ↦ L_p is UNIQUELY determined (L_h forced by tau_q j ∘ L_h ≈ S_h j ∘ tau_p j) has no in-tree counterpart, because the arrow part is simply supplied by fiat as `split`; (3) VOCABULARY — the reformulation E_p(Lim S) ≅ Lim(E_p S) cannot even be stated, since E_p is undefined in-tree (see maclane:V.3:construction1). The colimit dual is likewise absent.

gap: Missing: the general theorem for an arbitrary index category J — given S : J ⟶ [P, X] whose composites with each evaluation have limits, the construction of L : P ⟶ X with limiting cone tau in [P, X], plus the uniqueness of the arrow part of L.
